package_info.why_malicious: The package was intentionally published to npm to impersonate a legitimate local development example from React Native documentation. It collects sensitive system and user information and exfiltrates it to an external Discord webhook, constituting clear malicious data exfiltration.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or during postinstall, the code collects sensitive system and user information (home directory, username, DNS servers, hostnames, internal and external IPs, organization, and package metadata) and sends it to a hardcoded Discord webhook via HTTPS POST, enabling exfiltration of potentially sensitive developer and environment data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects a broad set of system and user information and exfiltrates it to an external service (Discord webhook) without user consent or legitimate purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package, especially one mimicking a documentation example, should not collect or transmit any user or system data externally. Normal behavior would be to provide only the documented functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or crash reporting tools may collect limited environment data, but always with user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Collection of home directory, username, and network information
Use of hardcoded external webhook for data exfiltration
No user notification or opt-in for telemetry
Impersonation of a documentation example to gain trust

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious npm package with the same name as a local example from official documentation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers are tricked into installing the malicious package via standard update commands.

attack_chain.action: Developer runs 'yarn upgrade rtn-centered-text', which fetches the malicious package from npm instead of using the local example.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is installed and executed in the developer's environment.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes at import-time or postinstall, collecting sensitive system and user data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is exfiltrated to a hardcoded Discord webhook.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive information from compromised environments.

behavioral_signatures: npm package collecting system/user/network information at install or import time
Outbound HTTPS requests to Discord webhooks or other hardcoded endpoints
Impersonation of package names from official documentation examples
file_indicators: index.js or main entry file containing os, dns, or network information gathering code
References to Discord webhook URLs in source code
Absence of legitimate package functionality (no README, no real exports)
network_indicators: Unexpected HTTPS POST requests during package install or import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that collect and transmit environment or user data to external endpoints, especially during install or import. Flag packages with hardcoded webhook URLs or those that match names of local development examples from documentation. Use static analysis to detect use of os, dns, and network modules in package entry points, and monitor for outbound requests to Discord or other suspicious domains during package installation.
